about: Training lines for docs/EXPERIMENTS_NATURAL.md (experiments.py). Each line is one training history and has its own folder, runs/natural/<folder>/, with one subfolder per piece (train.py --resume adds pieces; --line <folder> starts a new line). This file gives each line folder a display id, name, purpose ('tested') and result ('found'), and notes on pieces (keyed by the piece folder name). Edit freely, then run experiments.py.

lines.name: no jump, constant LR
lines.tested: Can PPO learn to chop trees in a generated world at all? First natural-world run, the arena's 11 actions.
lines.found: Yes, but modestly: 9.7 logs per episode at 503k (random spawns), 5.3x random actions.

lines.name: jump, constant LR
lines.tested: Does adding jump and forward_jump help on hilly terrain? Compare with Line 1.
lines.found: Yes: jump nearly doubled the score at ~500k (18.0 vs Line 1's 9.7, random spawns). With a constant LR it peaked near 600k (18.1 on fixed spots) and then got worse: 15.0 at 1M, -3.1 +/- 2.6 logs vs its 601k checkpoint spot by spot.

lines.name: linear LR from Line 2's 601k checkpoint
lines.tested: Line 2 slid from ~22 to ~15 logs between 600k and 1M at a constant learning rate. Does decaying the rate to 0 keep the gains?
lines.found: Yes: from the same 601k model it rose to 24.7 on fixed spots, while Line 2 fell to 15.0. Spot by spot: +6.7 +/- 3.1 logs over the split point and +9.8 +/- 3.5 over Line 2 @ 1M. Best model so far.

lines.name: jump, linear LR, from scratch
lines.tested: Line 2b's recipe in one consistent setup from step 0 (3 instances, render distance 4, linear LR). Does the patchwork history of 2b matter?
lines.found: No: 22.4 on fixed spots at 1M, tied with Line 2b (-2.3 +/- 3.0 spot by spot), with fewer 0-log episodes (6 vs 13). So 2b's result doesn't depend on its patchwork history.

lines.name: fine-tune Line 3 @ 1.0M for 500k more at a small LR
lines.tested: Line 3 ended with its learning rate at 0. Does 500k more steps at a small rate (5e-5 -> 0) still improve it, or is it at its limit with this setup?
lines.found: No: 21.9 on fixed spots at 1.5M, -0.5 +/- 3.1 logs vs Line 3 @ 1.0M spot by spot (better at 41 spots, worse at 51). The extra 500k steps changed nothing measurable; with this setup the model looks to be at its limit.

lines.name: 3M linear LR schedule, from Line 3 @ 257k
lines.tested: Line 3's 1M schedule stalled near 22 and fine-tuning (3b) didn't help. Does one longer schedule (2.29e-4 -> 0 over 257k -> 3M, as if a single 3M run) keep improving past 22? Also the first run with 4 instances (same 2048-step updates).
lines.found: No: 23.9 on fixed spots at 3M, tied with Line 3 @ 1M (+1.5 +/- 3.4 spot by spot, better at 47, worse at 48) and Line 2b (-0.8 +/- 3.5). At 1M, with its rate still high, it was behind Line 3 (16.1, -6.2 +/- 3.6) and then climbed back to the same level. Every recipe so far ends at ~22-25, so the limit is the setup, not training length.

lines.name: multi actions (move x turn x look x jump, attack held), linear LR, from scratch
lines.tested: Every single-action recipe ends at ~22-25 logs, so the limit looks like the setup. Do multi-choice actions (choose move, turn, look and jump every step, attack always held, exact-degree turns) beat Line 3's 22.4 at 1M with the same schedule? In the fixed arena they scored 31.3 vs 30.5 (3 runs each, not significant: the arena is near its 32 cap).
lines.found: Yes: 26.6 on fixed spots at 1M, the best so far. Spot by spot +4.2 +/- 3.0 logs vs Line 3 @ 1M (same recipe, only the actions differ; better at 57 spots, worse at 36) and +1.9 +/- 3.4 vs Line 2b (not significant). It learned slower early (training avg 15.4 vs Line 3's 20.3 at 330k-423k) but kept improving after Line 3 levelled off (29.8 vs 25.5 at 900k-1M).
